tagline: China's 'instant city' went from fishing villages to a 17-million tech metropolis in forty years — gadget megamarkets, drone shows and theme parks beside Hong Kong.
overview: Shenzhen is the city China built in a hurry. A sleepy border county of fishing villages until 1980, it became the country's first Special Economic Zone and exploded into a metropolis of some 17 million — home to the companies behind the phones, drones and gadgets in your pocket, from Huawei and Tencent to DJI.

The city rewards the curious: Huaqiangbei is the world's largest electronics market, a multi-block maze where anything with a circuit can be bought, built or fixed. Around it are design museums, the Ping An tower's observation deck and a string of beaches on the Dapeng Peninsula.

Speed visited on his 2025 China tour, drawn by the gadget markets and the city's drone-light spectacles. Between OCT Loft's art district and malls the size of towns, this is the future arriving early.

funFacts.title: AN INSTANT MEGACITY
funFacts.text: Shenzhen grew from ~30,000 people in 1980 to over 17 million — the fastest city growth ever recorded.

funFacts.title: SILICON VALLEY OF HARDWARE
funFacts.text: Huaqiangbei market is the world's biggest electronics bazaar — prototypes get built there in days.

funFacts.title: DRONE CAPITAL
funFacts.text: DJI, the world's dominant drone maker, is headquartered in Shenzhen.

funFacts.title: 130 LANDMARKS IN ONE PARK
funFacts.text: Window of the World squeezes replicas of 130 global icons into a single theme park.

funFacts.title: HONG KONG'S NEIGHBOUR
funFacts.text: The Hong Kong border is minutes away by metro or high-speed rail.

funFacts.title: A CITY OF TWENTYSOMETHINGS

funFacts.title: SKY-BRIDGE TOWERS

funFacts.title: CITY BEACHES

funFacts.title: AN URBAN RAINFOREST
